decisions.context: The classifier receives millions of documents daily, so ingestion must handle sustained high volume. The brief gives no latency requirement.
decisions.rationale: Batch ingestion suits the stated volume, and the brief does not require immediate results (d:7, v:7.3). The batch design point had no warnings; it was unattested, as was the streaming rival.
consequences: Tune batch size and cadence to volume.

decisions.context: Document volume varies strongly over the year, requiring a processing approach that can manage large workloads. The brief does not specify real-time classification.
decisions.rationale: Batch processing matches the high, variable volume without assuming a latency need absent from the brief (d:15, v:15.1). The batch design point had no warnings; it was unattested, as was the streaming rival.

decisions.context: Several teams consume predictions, and the brief does not require synchronous responses. A shared result store can support scheduled batch delivery.
decisions.rationale: Scheduled batch predictions stored for access fit the stated consumers and volume without introducing an unstated real-time requirement (d:5, v:5.3). The batch design point had no warnings; it was unattested, as was the real-time rival.
consequences: Consumers read results from shared storage.
Define result ownership and freshness expectations.

decisions.context: Operators need to see when classification quality drifts. That calls for monitoring model performance in production.

alternatives.label: Monitoring or logging data and predictions
cons: Logs alone may not show quality

decisions.rationale: Performance monitoring directly addresses the brief’s requirement to expose quality drift (d:22, v:22.1). The chosen batch design point had no warnings and was unattested; the streaming rival was also unattested.
consequences: Choose quality measures and alert thresholds.
Monitoring depends on timely quality signals.

uncovered: Autoscaling and capacity planning for seasonal volume.
